## Setup

There is no setup recipe yet. A fresh checkout or worktree runs `npm ci`, then
`node tools/fetch-luau.mjs`, which provisions the pinned Luau 0.743 development runtime
the Noctalia plugin's contract tests (`integrations/noctalia-plugin/`) run under. It
verifies the release archive's SHA-256 and writes
`node_modules/.cache/familiar-luau/0.743/luau`; `--archive <zip>` uses a local copy. CI
does the same; a missing runtime fails those tests with this hint rather than skipping.
Install the hooks in a fresh clone with `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`.

## Gates

Every recipe records its wall time through `tools/tt`. `just test-fast` runs the fast
partition (`npm test`, i.e. `tools/test-runner.mjs fast`: everything but
`*.slow.test.js`); `just test` runs it and then the slow partition, the real-tmux pty
test, which needs tmux and util-linux `script`. `just check` is the pre-commit gate:
`tools/ops-check`, `tools/ops-docs check` and `tasks check`. `just gate` is the
pre-push one, check plus the full suite. `just docs` regenerates the identity and
family regions of README.md and AGENTS.md from identity.toml and tools/family.toml;
never edit inside those regions.

## Layout

- `bin/`: launchers and CLI implementations; `src/`: the engine.
- `integrations/`: Niri, Noctalia and OpenCode plugins.
- `test/`: the suite; `tools/test-runner.mjs` runs it in isolated workers.
- `tools/`: test and gate helpers, plus ops tooling vendored as exact copies
  (tools/README.md); never edit a vendored copy.

## Rules

- `bin/familiar` and `bin/familiar-opencode` are launchers: they call
  `requireDependencies()` from `src/deps.js` and then dynamically import the
  implementation beside them (`bin/familiar.js`, `bin/familiar-opencode.js`). A missing
  bare specifier fails at resolution, before any module runs, so a check inside those
  files could never report it. Keep the launchers importing nothing but `src/deps.js`,
  and add new CLI code to the `.js` implementations.
- `bin/familiar.js` is the CLI's front door: parsing, help, completion and routing. It
  runs `observe` (every hook event, and SessionEnd under relay's tightest teardown budget)
  by loading `src/observe/run.js` alone, and loads `bin/familiar-commands.js` for every
  other command. Add command code there, not to the front door, and keep the theme
  contract, YAML and the visual modules off a SessionEnd's path:
  `test/bin-familiar.test.js` traces what a teardown loads. `statusline`, polled for every
  open session, checks its per-session render cache (`src/render/term/render-cache.js`) in
  the front door and loads `renderStatusline` from `bin/familiar-commands.js` only on a
  miss. Anything new the HUD shows must come through `readFields`, which the key covers.
- The theme contract lives in the `familiar-theme` package (git dependency);
  do not deep-import beyond its package export.
- Pre-split history and design docs: https://github.com/khughitt/familiar-archive (private archive)
- Design specs and implementation plans live in the records root (`tasks where` names it);
  `docs/specs/`, `docs/plans/` and `docs/notes/` keep only those the code cites.
- Before completion, run `tasks check`. Require zero errors and report every warning. Registration-only `unreachable_dep` and `cycle_unverifiable` warnings are environmental on machines without all referenced projects; resolve every other warning.
